Definition: from the same as G2947; rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands):--maimed.
BiblicalUsage: Maimed is the word for a body broken in hand or foot, and Jesus uses it both ways. In Matthew 15:30 the maimed are brought to Him and healed, and the multitude wonders in Matthew 15:31 when they see "the maimed to be whole"; but in Mark 9:43 and Matthew 18:8 He says it is better to enter into life maimed than with two hands to go into hell.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that Jesus means both sayings at once: He heals the maimed here, and He warns that a hand is not worth hell, and the mercy and the warning come from the same mouth. He heals the maimed, and He warns the whole: both are mercy.
